text: 壽永三年二月七日、攝津國一谷にて討れし平氏の頸共十二日に都へ入る。平家に結ぼほれたる人々は、我方樣に、如何なる憂目をか見んずらんと歎きあひ悲みあへり。中にも大覺寺に隱れ居給る小松三位中將維盛卿の北の方殊更覺束なく思はれける。今度一谷にて一門の人々殘り少ううたれ給ひ、三位中將と云ふ公卿一人生捕にせられて上るなりと聞給ひ、此人離れじ物をとて、引覆てぞ伏給ふ。或女房の出來て申けるは、「三位中將殿と申は、是の御事にて候はず。本三位中將殿の御事也。」と申ければ、「さては頸共の中にこそあるらめ。」とて、猶心安も思ひ給はず。同十三日、大夫判官仲頼、六條河原に出向て、頸共請取。東洞院の大路を北へ渡して、獄門の木に懸らるべき由、蒲冠者範頼九郎冠者義經奏聞す。法皇此條いかがあるべからむと思召し煩ひて、太政大臣、左右の大臣、内大臣、堀河大納言忠親卿に仰合せらる。五人の公卿申されけるは、「昔より卿相の位に上るものの頸、大路を渡さるゝ事先例なし。就中、此輩は先帝の御時戚里の臣として、久く朝家に事つる。範頼義經が申状、あながち御許容有べからず。」とおの／＼一同に申されければ、渡さるまじきにて有けるを、範頼義經重ねて奏聞しけるは、「保元の昔を思へば、祖父爲義が讐、平治の古を案ずれば、父義朝が敵也。君の御憤を息め奉り、父祖の恥を雪めんが爲に命を棄て、朝敵を滅す。今度平氏の頸共、大路を渡されずば、自今以後何のいさみ有てか、凶賊を退けんや。」と、兩人頻に訴へ申間、法皇力及ばせ給はで、遂に渡されけり。見る人幾等と云ふ數を知らず。帝闕に袖をつらねし古へは、恐怖るゝ輩多かりき。巷に首を渡さるゝ今は哀み悲しまずと云ふ事なし。

annotation.translation: In the third year of Juei, on the seventh day of the second month, the twelve heads of the Taira clan, slain at Hitotani in Settsu Province, were brought into the capital on the twelfth. The people who had been attached to the Taira family sighed and wept together, saying, 'What a miserable sight we shall see in this manner!' Among them, the Northern Lady of the young nobleman Minamoto no Norimori, the Third Rank Junior Captain, who was residing in seclusion at Daikaku-ji, was thought to be particularly distraught. It was heard that this time, at Hitotani, most of the Taira family members had been killed, and only one court noble, known as the Third Rank Junior Captain, had been captured alive and brought here. Because he was someone they could not leave behind, they drew their robes over their heads and bowed down. Then, a lady-in-waiting came forward and said, 'The title Third Rank Junior Captain is not appropriate in this matter. It concerns the actual Third Rank Junior Captain.' Upon hearing this, they said, 'Then he must be among the heads.' Yet they still felt no peace of mind. On the thirteenth day, Dainagon Nakayori and Rokujō Kawara went out to claim the heads. They crossed the main east-west avenue of Higashi-Tōin to the north, and the priest Kamo no Noriyori and the priest Kamo no Yoshitsune, both titled Kyōju, reported to the Emperor that the heads should be hung on the execution posts. The Retired Emperor, pondering how this could be allowed, consulted with the Daijō-daijin, the Ministers of the Left and Right, the Udaijin, and the Dainagon Horikawa, Tadahide. The five court nobles replied, 'There is no precedent from ancient times for the heads of any person who has risen to the rank of minister or above to be carried across a main avenue. Especially, these men served as relatives of the imperial family during the reign of the late Emperor, serving the imperial court for a long time. The petition submitted by Noriyori and Yoshitsune cannot possibly be permitted.' When they all spoke in unison that the heads should not be carried across, Noriyori and Yoshitsune repeatedly reported again, 'If we think of the times of Hōgen, the grandfather Tameyori was our enemy; if we consider the past of Heiji, the father Yoshitomo was our foe. We have laid down our lives to appease the Emperor's anger and to avenge the shame of our ancestors by destroying the enemies of the court. If the heads of the Taira clan this time are not carried across the main avenue, how will anyone from now on dare to drive out such wicked bandits?' As the two men pleaded repeatedly, the Retired Emperor, unable to stop them, finally allowed the heads to be carried across. The number of those who looked on was countless. In ancient times, when the imperial palace was lined with sleeves, there were many who felt terror. Now, when heads are carried across the streets, there is no one who does not mourn and weep.'

text: 小松三位中將維盛卿の若君六代御前に附たてまつたる齋藤五、齋藤六、あまりの覺束なさに、樣を窶して見ければ、頸共は見知り奉たれども、三位中將殿の御頸は見え給はず。されども餘に悲しくて、つゝむに堪へぬ涙のみ滋かりければ、餘所の人目も怖しさに、急ぎ大覺寺へぞ參ける。北方、「さて如何にやいかに。」と問給へば、「小松殿の君達には備中守殿の御頸ばかりこそ見えさせ給ひ候つれ。其外はそんぢやう其頸其御頸。」と申ければ、「いづれも人の上とも覺えず。」とて、涙に咽び給けり。良有て、齋藤五涙を抑へて申けるは、「此一兩年は隱居候て、人にもいたく見知れ候はず。今暫も見參すべう候つれども、よにくはしう案内知り參せたる者の申候つるは、『小松殿の君達は今度の合戰には、播磨と丹波の境で候なる三草山を固めさせ給ひて候けるが、九郎義經に破られて、新三位中將殿、小松少將殿、丹波侍從殿は、播磨の高砂より御船に召して、讃岐の八島へ渡らせ給て候也。何として離れさせ給ひて候けるやらん。御兄弟の御中に備中守殿ばかり一谷にて討れさせ給ひて候。』と申者にこそ逢ひて候つれ。『さて三位中將殿の御事は如何に。』と問候つれば、『其は軍已前より大事の御痛とて、八島に御渡候間、此度は向はせ給候はず。』と、細々とこそ申候つれ。」と申ければ、「其も我等が事をあまりに思嘆き給ふが、病と成たるにこそ。風の吹日は今日もや船に乘り給らんと肝を消し、軍といふ時は、唯今もや討たれ給らんと心を盡す。ましてさ樣の痛なんどをも、誰か心安うも扱ひ奉るべき。委しう聞ばや。」と宣へば、若君姫君「など何の御痛りとは問はざりけるぞ。」と宣ひけるこそあはれなれ。

annotation.translation: Saito Go and Saito Roku, who had been attached as attendants to the young lord, the sixth generation, before His Majesty the Emperor, were so unsteady in their appearance that, after looking at them closely, although they recognized the necks of others, they did not see the neck of the Dainagon, Lord Minamoto no Tomomori. Yet, because they were overcome with such sorrow that they could not hold back their tears, fearing the gaze of others, they hurriedly went to the Daikaku-ji Temple. The Northern Lord asked, "Well, what shall be done?" When he replied, "Only the neck of the Bitchu-no-kami was made visible to the Lord's children of Komatsu; as for the rest, that was so: that neck, that imperial neck," the Northern Lord said, "Neither of them could be distinguished as humans," and wept, choked with tears. Then, Saito Go, suppressing his tears, said, "For the past one or two years, I have lived in seclusion and have not been known to anyone. Although I may now be permitted to pay a visit, I met someone who had thoroughly learned the details and reported, 'The Lord's children of Komatsu have fortified the Three Grass Mountains, which lie on the border of Bizen and Tanba, for this battle, but were defeated by Kurando Yoshitsune. The Shin-Dainagon, the Komatsu Shono, and the Tanba Shojun were summoned from Takasaka in Bizen to their ships and sent across to the Hachima in Sanuki. How could they have been allowed to separate? Only the Bitchu-no-kami was slain at Hitotani among the imperial brothers.' When I asked, 'What of the matter concerning the Dainagon?' he replied, 'Since before the war began, he has been suffering from a serious illness, and since he has already crossed to Hachima, he has not been allowed to return this time.' Thus, he reported in detail." When he said this, the Northern Lord declared, "It is because you are thinking too much of our affairs that you have fallen ill. On days when the wind blows, I wonder if I will board the ship today; when there is a battle, I worry that I will be slain right now. How much more so, then, could anyone calmly deal with such an illness? I would like to hear the details." Upon hearing this, the young prince and princess said, "Why did you not ask what illness he had?" Such was the pitiful scene.

text: 三位中將も、通ふ心なれば、「都に如何に覺束なく思ふらん、頸共の中にはなくとも、水に溺ても死に、矢に當ても失ぬらん、此世に在者とは、よも思はじ。露の命のいまだながらへたると知らせ奉らばや。」とて、侍一人したてて都へのぼらせけり。三の文をぞ書かれける。先北方への御文には、「都には敵滿々て、御身一の置所だにあらじに、幼き者共引具して、如何にかなしう覺すらん。是へ迎奉て、一所でいかにもならばやとは思へども、我身こそあらめ、御爲こゝろぐるしくて。」など、細々と書續け、奧に一首の歌ぞありける。

annotation.translation: The Chūnagon also, being of a mind to pass through, said, 'How forlorn must you feel in the capital? Even if not among your necks, you will not die by drowning, nor be struck by an arrow; you surely do not think you are in this world. If it were to be known that your dew-like lives have not yet perished, how wonderful!' Thus, he stationed one attendant and sent him up to the capital. He wrote three letters. In the imperial letter to the north beforehand, it was written, 'In the capital, the enemy is everywhere, and there is not even a place for your Majesty to stay. Though I thought to lead the young ones and welcome them here, so that we might be together, I myself must be there, for I am deeply concerned for your sake,' and so on, he wrote in detail, and there was a poem within.

text: 少き人々の御許へは、「つれ％＼をば如何にしてか慰み給ふらん。急ぎ迎へ取らんずるぞ。」と、言の葉もかはらず書いて上せられけり。此御文共を給はて使都へ上り、北方に御文參せたりければ、今更又嘆き悲み給ひけり。使四五日候て暇申。北方泣々御返事かき給ふ。若君姫君筆をそめて、「さて父御前の御返事は何と申べきやらん。」と問給へば、「唯ともかうも和御前達の思はん樣に申べし。」とこそ宣ひけれ。「などや今まで迎へさせ給はぬぞ、あまりに戀しく思ひ參せ候に、とくとく迎させ給へ。」と、同じ言葉にぞかゝれたる、此御文共を給はて、使八島に歸りまゐる。三位中將殿先少人々の御文を御覽じてこそ、彌詮方なげには見えられけれ。「抑是より穢土を厭ふに勇なし。閻浮愛執の綱つよければ、淨土を願ふも懶し。唯是より山傳ひに都へ上て戀き者共を今一度見もし見えて後、自害をせんにはしかじ。」とぞ、泣々語給ひける。

annotation.translation: To the younger ones: 'How will you comfort yourselves in your sorrow? I shall hasten to welcome you.' Such words were written without change. These letters were sent to the capital, and when they were delivered to the Northern Lady, she sighed and wept anew. The messenger waited four or five days and then reported the matter. The Northern Lady, in tears, wrote a reply. The young lord and the princess dipped their brushes and asked, 'Now, what shall we say in reply to our father?' 'We must speak as my mother and her ladies-in-waiting wish,' was the reply. 'Why have you not allowed us to be welcomed until now? We have longed for you so deeply; please welcome us without delay.' Being caught by the same words, these letters were sent, and the messenger returned to the Eight Islands. The Lady of the Third Rank and the Middle Captain read the letters of the younger ones and were deeply moved. 'Indeed, from now on I have no courage to loathe this defiled world. The bonds of love and attachment in Jambudvipa are too strong; even to wish for the Pure Land is tedious. From now on, I shall travel over the mountains to the capital, see once more those I love, and then commit suicide.' Thus she spoke, in tears.

text: 同十四日、生捕本三位中將重衡卿、六條を東へわたされけり。小八葉の車に前後の簾を上げ、左右の物見を開く。土肥次郎實平、木蘭地の直垂に小具足許して、隨兵三十餘騎、車の前後に打圍で守護し奉る。京中の貴賤是を見て、「あないとほし、如何なる罪の報ぞや。いくらも在ます君達の中に、かく成給ふ事よ。入道殿にも二位殿にも、おぼえの御子にてましまししかば、御一家の人々も重き事に思ひ奉り給ひしぞかし。院へも内へも參り給ひし時は、老たるも若きも、所をおきて持成奉り給ひしものを。是は南都を滅し給へる伽藍の罰にこそ。」と申あへり。河原迄渡されて、かへて、故中御門藤中納言家成卿の八條堀河の御堂に居奉て、土肥次郎守護し奉る。院御所より御使に藏人左衞門權佐定長、八條堀河へ向はれけり。赤衣に劍笏をぞ帶したる。三位中將は、紺村濃の直垂に、立烏帽子引立ておはします。日頃は何とも思れざりし定長を、今は冥途にて罪人共が、冥官に逢る心地ぞせられける。仰下されけるは、「八島へ歸りたくば、一門の中へ言送て、三種神器を都へ返し入れ奉れ。然らば八島へ返さるべきとの御氣色で候。」と申。三位中將申されけるは、「重衡千人萬人が命にも、三種の神器を替參せんとは内府己下一門の者共一人もよも申候はじ。もし女性にて候へば、母儀の二品なんどや、さも申候はんずらん。さは候へども居ながら院宣を返し參らせん事、其恐も候へば、申送てこそ見候はめ。」とぞ申されける。御使は、平三左衞門重國、御坪の召次花方とぞ聞えし。私の文は容れねば、人々の許へも詞にて言づけ給ふ。北方大納言佐殿へも、御詞にて申されけり。「旅の空にても、人は我に慰み、我は人に慰み奉りしに、引別れて後、如何に悲しうおぼすらん。契は朽せぬものと申せば、後の世には必生れあひ奉らん。」と、泣泣言づけ給へば、重國も、涙を抑へて立にけり。

annotation.translation: On the fourteenth of that same month, the living capture of the Vice-Minister of the Third Rank, Prince Shigehira, was ordered, and he was sent across to Rokujō. The curtains at the front and rear of the carriage of the Eight Leaves were raised, and the side viewing panels were opened. Doi Jirō Sanehira, wearing a wooden-sleeved robe over his armor, with thirty-odd retainers, surrounded the carriage at the front and rear and guarded him respectfully. Those of high and low rank in the capital, upon seeing this, said, "How terrible, how terrible! What retribution for what sin? Among so many lords who are still alive, how can such a thing happen? Since the Emperor-Insei and the Second Rank were his fathers of noble birth, the members of his own family too must have thought this a grave matter. When he had visited the Retired Emperor's residence or the Inner Palace, whether old or young, all had respectfully supported him wherever he went. This must be the punishment of the temples he destroyed in the Southern Capital," they said. He was ferried as far as the riverbank, then was returned and made to reside in the palace of the late Chancellor of State Fujiwara no Ienari at Hachijō Horikawa, where Doi Jirō guarded him. An envoy was sent from the Imperial Palace: Kura no Shōemon Gon-no-Suke Norinaga, heading for Hachijō Horikawa. He wore a red robe and carried a sword and a baton. The Vice-Minister of the Third Rank, Prince Shigehira, stood supported, wearing a dark blue robe and a black formal cap. Norinaga, whom he had never thought anything of in former days, now felt as if he were meeting a judge of the underworld among sinners on the road to the netherworld. Norinaga said, "If you wish to return to the Eight Islands, send a message to your clan and return the Three Sacred Treasures to the capital. Then you will be permitted to return to the Eight Islands." The Vice-Minister of the Third Rank replied, "Even if a thousand or ten thousand men were to offer their lives, I would not exchange the Three Sacred Treasures for them. Not even one person among the Inner Court and the Imperial Clan would say such a thing. If I were a woman, I might say such things, as my mother held the Second Rank. Nevertheless, to return the Imperial Edict while I am still alive is something I fear to do; therefore, I must send a message to you to see." The envoy was said to be Taira no Sanzaemon Shigenori, known as the flower of the Imperial Court's attendants. If my letter is not accepted, he will deliver a message to others in person. He also delivered a message to the Northern Minister of the Left, Sado, in person. "Even in the empty sky of travel, people comforted me, and I comforted people; after we are parted, how sorrowful it will seem. If the vow is said to be imperishable, then in the next life we shall surely be born together," he wept and sent his message. Shigenori, holding back his tears, stood there."

Since the Emperor-Insei and the Second Rank were his fathers of noble birth, the members of his own family too must have thought this a grave matter. When he had visited the Retired Emperor's residence or the Inner Palace, whether old or young, all had respectfully supported him wherever he went. This must be the punishment of the temples he destroyed in the Southern Capital," they said. He was ferried as far as the riverbank, then was returned and made to reside in the palace of the late Chancellor of State Fujiwara no Ienari at Hachijō Horikawa, where Doi Jirō guarded him. An envoy was sent from the Imperial Palace: Kura no Shōemon Gon-no-Suke Norinaga, heading for Hachijō Horikawa. He wore a red robe and carried a sword and a baton. The Vice-Minister of the Third Rank, Prince Shigehira, stood supported, wearing a dark blue robe and a black formal cap. Norinaga, whom he had never thought anything of in former days, now felt as if he were meeting a judge of the underworld among sinners on the road to the netherworld. Norinaga said, "If you wish to return to the Eight Islands, send a message to your clan and return the Three Sacred Treasures to the capital. Then you will be permitted to return to the Eight Islands." The Vice-Minister of the Third Rank replied, "Even if a thousand or ten thousand men were to offer their lives, I would not exchange the Three Sacred Treasures for them. Not even one person among the Inner Court and the Imperial Clan would say such a thing. If I were a woman, I might say such things, as my mother held the Second Rank. Nevertheless, to return the Imperial Edict while I am still alive is something I fear to do; therefore, I must send a message to you to see." The envoy was said to be Taira no Sanzaemon Shigenori, known as the flower of the Imperial Court's attendants. If my letter is not accepted, he will deliver a message to others in person. He also delivered a message to the Northern Minister of the Left, Sado, in person. "Even in the empty sky of travel, people comforted me, and I comforted people; after we are parted, how sorrowful it will seem. If the vow is said to be imperishable, then in the next life we shall surely be born together," he wept and sent his message. Shigenori, holding back his tears, stood there."

text: 三位中將の年比召仕はれける侍に木工右馬允知時といふ者あり。八條女院に候けるが、土肥次郎が許に行向て、「是は中將殿に先年召仕れ候し某と申す者にて候が、西國へも御供仕べき由存候しかども、八條の女院に兼參の者にて候間、力及ばで罷留て候が、今日大路で見參せ候へば、目も當られず、いとほしう思奉り候。然るべう候はゞ御許されを蒙て、近附參候て、今一度見參に入り、昔語をも申て、なぐさめ參せばやと存候。させる弓矢取る身で候はねば、軍合戰の御供を仕たる事も候はず、只朝夕祇候せしばかりで候き。さりながら猶覺束なう思食し候はば、腰の刀を召置れて、まげて御許されを蒙候はばや。」と申せば、土肥次郎情ある男士にて、「御一人ばかりは何事か候べき。さりながらも。」とて、腰の刀を乞取て入てけり。右馬允斜ならず悦で、急ぎ參て見奉れば、誠に思ひ入れ給へると覺しくて、御姿もいたくしをれ返て居給へる御有樣を見奉るに、知時涙も更に抑へ難し。三位中將も是を御覽じて夢に夢見る心地して、とかうの事も宣まはず。只泣より外の事ぞなき。稍久しう有て、昔今の物語共し給ひて後、「さても汝して物言し人は、未だ内裏にとや聞く。」「さこそ承り候へ。」「西國へ下りし時、文をもやらず、いひおく事だに無りしを、世々の契は、皆僞にて有けりと思ふらんこそ慚かしけれ。文をやらばやと思ふは如何に、尋て行てんや。」と宣へば、「御文を給て參り候はん。」と申す。中將斜ならず悦て、やがて書てぞたうだりける。守護の武士共、「如何なる御文にて候やらん。出し參せじ。」と申。中將「見せよ。」と宣へば、見せてけり。「苦しう候まじ。」とて、取らせけり。知時持て、内裏へ參りたりけれども、晝は人目の繁ければ、其邊近き小屋に立入て、日を待暮し、局の下口邊にたゝずんで聞けば、此人の聲と覺しくて、「いくらもある人の中に三位中將しも生捕にせられて大路を渡さるゝ事よ。人は皆奈良を燒たる罪の報と言あへり。中將も、さぞ云し。『我心に起ては燒ねども、惡黨多かりしかば、手々に火を放て、おほくの常塔を燒拂ふ。末の露本の雫と成なれば、我一人が罪にこそならんずらめ。』といひしが、げにさと覺ゆる。」と掻口説きさめざめとぞ泣れける。右馬允、是にも思はれけるものをといとほしくおぼえて、「物申さう。」といへば、「いづくより。」と問給ふ。「三位中將殿より御文の候。」と申せば、年比は恥て見え給はぬ女房の、せめての思ひの餘にや「いづらやいづら。」とて走出でて、手づから文を取て見給へば、西國よりとられてありし有樣、今日明日とも知らぬ身の行末など、細々と書續け、奧には一首の歌ぞ有ける。

annotation.translation: There was a samurai named Takaji, the Right Horse Attendant of the Wood Department, who had served the Third Rank Middle Captain for many years. He was in attendance upon the Lady of the Eight-Street Imperial Residence, but he went to the residence of Doi Jiro, saying, 'I am one who formerly served the Middle Captain; although I intended to accompany him to the Western Provinces, I was detained here as a permanent attendant of the Eight-Street Lady, and was unable to go. However, as I have come to see him today on the main road, I am utterly unable to face him, and my heart is filled with sorrow. If it may be permitted, I wish to come near, to see him once more, to speak of old times, and perhaps to offer some comfort.' 'I am not one to draw a bow or hold a sword,' he continued, 'nor have I ever served in the ranks of war; I have merely attended day and night. Yet, if I still feel uneasy, I shall take my sword from my waist, prostrate myself before you, and beg your permission.' Doi Jiro, a man of great feeling, replied, 'Is there any harm in allowing just one person? Nevertheless,' he said, and took the sword from the samurai's waist, entering with it. The Right Horse Attendant was exceedingly pleased; hurrying to see, he perceived that the Lady had indeed deeply cared for him, and seeing her figure, so utterly changed and sitting there, he could no longer restrain his tears. The Third Rank Middle Captain, viewing this, felt as though in a dream, and uttered no words of such a thing; there was nothing but weeping. After a while, having spoken of past and present events, he said, 'I hear that you are still in the Imperial Palace. I have heard so. When I descended to the Western Provinces, I sent no letter, nor did I leave any message; I fear that all the vows of generations were mere falsehoods. How would you feel if I were to send a letter? Would you not seek me out?' 'I shall receive your letter,' he replied. The Middle Captain, exceedingly pleased, immediately wrote it. The guardian warriors asked, 'What sort of letter is this? We shall not allow it to be shown.' The Middle Captain said, 'Show it.' So they showed it. 'It shall not be a burden,' they said, and took it away. Takaji carried it to the Imperial Palace, but since the daytime was crowded with people, he entered a small hut nearby, waited until evening, and stood near the lower entrance of the chamber. Hearing the voice, he thought, 'It is this person. The Third Rank Middle Captain has been captured alive and is being led across the main road. Everyone says this is the retribution for the crime of burning Nara. The Middle Captain surely said this: "Though my heart burns within, there were so many evil bandits that I ordered the fires to be set one by one, and burned the great pagodas. When the final dew becomes a drop, let my single guilt suffice."' So he said, and now it truly seemed clear. He spoke persuasively, weeping bitterly. The Right Horse Attendant, thinking, 'He too feels this,' said, 'I have something to say.' 'From where?' asked the Middle Captain. 'From the Third Rank Middle Captain, a letter,' he replied. The woman of long-standing service, now ashamed to appear, moved by the depth of her feelings, said, 'Where, where?' and rushed out, taking the letter in her own hands to read. It described in detail how she had been taken from the Western Provinces, and the uncertain fate of her body today and tomorrow, and in the end, there was a single poem.

text: 知時持て、參りたり。守護の武士共、又「見參せ候はん。」と申せば、見せてけり。「苦しう候まじ。」とて奉る。三位中將是を見て、彌思や増り給ひけん、土肥次郎に宣ひけるは、「年比相具したりし女房に、今一度對面して、申たき事の有るは如何がすべき。」と宣へば、實平情ある士にて、「誠に女房などの御事にて渡らせ給ひ候はんはなじかは苦う候べき。」とて許し奉る。中將斜ならず悦て、人に車借て迎へに遣したりければ、女房取もあへず、是に乘てぞおはしける。縁に車をやり寄せてかくと申せば、中將車寄に出迎ひ給ひ、「武士共の見奉るに、下させ給べからず。」とて、車の簾を打かつぎ、手に手を取組み、顏に顏を推當てて、暫しは物も宣はず、唯泣より外の事ぞなき。稍久しう有て、中將宣ひけるは、「西國へ下し時も、今一度見參せたう候しかども、大形の世の騒さに申べき便もなくて、罷下り候ぬ。其後はいかにもして御文をも參らせ、御返り事をも承はりたう候しかども、心に任せぬ旅の習ひ、明暮の軍に隙なくて、空しく年月を送り候き。今又人知ぬ在樣を見候は再あひ奉るべきで候けり。」とて、袖を顏に推當てうつぶしにぞなられける。互の心の中、推量られてあはれ也。かくて小夜も半に成ければ、「此ごろは大路の狼藉に候に、疾々。」と返し奉る。車遣出せば、中將別れの涙を押へて泣々袖を引へつゝ、

annotation.translation: I have arrived, I have come. The guard samurai said, 'You shall appear before us again.' He showed himself. 'It shall not be painful,' he said, and presented himself. The Sanmi no Chujo, seeing this, thought, 'How shall I manage to meet once more with the lady who has been with me for so many years and have something to tell her?' He said to Tobi no Jiro: 'It is a matter of a lady; it would not be painful to send her over, would it?' Sanehira, a man of deep feeling, replied, 'Indeed, it would be no trouble to send her over.' The Chujo, greatly pleased, had a carriage borrowed and sent someone to fetch her. The lady, unable to refuse, boarded it. When the carriage was brought close to the veranda, she said, 'Please hide.' The Chujo came out to meet her in the carriage, saying, 'The samurai must not see us.' He raised the curtain of the carriage, took her hand in his, pressed his face against hers, and for a while said nothing at all, only weeping. After a long time, the Chujo spoke: 'Even when I went down to the Western Provinces, I wished to appear before you once more, but amidst the tumult of the great age, there was no opportunity to speak, and I did not come down. Since then, I have wanted to send you a letter and receive your reply, but the habit of travel, which cannot be controlled by the heart, and the ceaseless day and night of warfare left no time, and I have spent the years in vain. Now, seeing you in a manner unknown to others, I must meet you again.' He pressed his sleeve to his face and fell weeping. The feelings in their hearts were mutually understood, and it was most moving. Thus, when the moon had reached its half, she replied, 'These days are filled with the lawlessness of the great road; quickly.' When the carriage driver was sent out, the Chujo, holding back his tears of parting, wept and pulled at her sleeve as he said,

text:
大臣殿、平大納言の許へは院宣の趣を申給ふ。二位殿へは御文細々と書いて進らせられたり。「今一度御覽ぜんと思めし候はゞ内侍所の御事を大臣殿によく／＼申させおはしませ。さ候はでは此世にて見參に入べしとも覺え候はず。」などぞ書れたる。二位殿は是を見給ひてとかうの事も宣はず、文を懷に引入てうつぶしにぞなられける。
誠に心の中さこそおはしけめと推量られて哀也。さる程に平大納言時忠卿をはじめと
して平家一門の公卿殿上人寄合ひ給ひて御請文の趣僉議せらる。二位殿は中將の文を
顏に推當てゝ、人々の並居給へる後の障子を引明て、大臣殿の御前に倒臥し、泣々宣
ひけるは「あの中將が京より言おこしたる事の無慚さよ。げにも心の中にいかばかり
の事をか思ひ居たるらん。唯我に思ひ許して内侍所を、都へ入奉れ。」と宣へば、大
臣殿、「誠に宗盛もさこそは存候へども、さすが世の聞えもいふがひなう候。且は頼朝が思はん事もはづかしう候へば、左右なう内侍所を返し入奉る事は叶ひ候まじ。其上帝王の世を保せ給ふ御事は、偏に内侍所の御故也。子の悲いも樣にこそ依候へ。且は中將一人に餘の子共親しい人々をば思食替させ給ふべきか。」と申されければ、二位殿、重て宣ひけるは、「故入道におくれて後は、かた時も命生て、在べしとも思はざりしかども、主上かやうにいつとなく、旅だゝせ給たる御事の御心苦しさ、又、君をも御代にあらせ參せばやと思ふ故にこそ今迄もながらへて在つれ。中將一谷で生捕にせられぬと聞し後は肝魂も身に副はず、如何にもして此世にて今一度あひ見るべきと思へども、夢にだに見えねば、いとどむねせきて、湯水も喉へ入れられず。今この文を見て後は、彌思ひ遣たる方もなし。中將世になき者と聞かば、我も同じ道に赴むかんと思ふ也。再び物を思はせぬ先に、唯我を失ひ給へ。」とて、喚き叫び給へば、誠にさこそは思ひ給らめとあはれに覺えて、人々泪を流しつゝ皆伏目にぞなられける。新中納言知盛の意見に申されけるは、「三種の神器を都へ返入奉たりとも、重衡を返し給らん事有がたし。唯憚なく其樣を、御請文に申さるべうや候らん。」と申されければ、大臣殿「此儀尤も然るべし。」とて、御請文申されけり。二位殿は泣々中將の御返事かき給ひけるが、涙にくれて、筆の立所も覺ねども、志をしるべにて御文細々と書て重國にたびにけり。北方大納言佐殿は、唯泣より外の事なくて、つや／＼御返事もし給はず。誠に御心の中さこそは思ひ給らめと推量られてあはれ也。重國も狩衣の袖を絞りつゝ泣泣御前を罷り立つ。平大納言時忠は御坪召次花方を召て、「汝は花方か。」「さん候。」「法皇の御使に、多くの浪路を凌いで、是迄參りたるに一期が間の思出一つあるべし。」とて花方が面に、浪方と云ふ燒驗をぞせられける。都へ上りければ、法皇是を御覽じて、「好々力およばず、浪方とも召せかし。」とてわらはせおはします。

annotation.translation: The Minister told the Emperor's decree to the Heike Dainagon, and wrote a letter in fine characters to send to the Lady-in-Waiting. It read: 'If you wish to see once more, please have the Minister explain the affairs of the Inner Palace thoroughly. If you do so, you may be allowed to see this world again.' The Lady-in-Waiting read this letter, did not speak of such matters, and, taking the letter into her bosom, fell face down. It was truly pitiable, as one could only imagine the depth of her sorrow. At that time, the Heike Dainagon Tokutaka, along with the court nobles of the Heike clan, gathered to deliberate on the content of the petition. The Lady-in-Waiting held the General's letter to her face, then pulled aside the shoji screen where the people were standing and collapsed before the Minister, weeping and saying, 'The shamelessness of that General's actions sent from the capital! Truly, how much must he have thought within his heart? Only allow me to send the Inner Palace to the capital.' 三位中將是を聞て、「さこそは有むずれ。如何に一門の人々惡く思ひけん。」と、後悔すれどもかひぞなき。げにも重衡卿一人を惜みて、さしもの我朝の重寶三種の神器を、返し入れ奉るべしとも覺えねば、此御請文の趣は、兼てより思ひ設られたりしかども、未左右を申されざりつる程は、何となういぶせく思はれけるに、請文既に到來して、關東へ下向せらるべきに定まりしかば、何の憑も弱り果て萬心細う都の名殘も今更惜思はれける。三位中將土肥次郎を召て、「出家をせばやと思ふは如何あるべ
き。」と宣へば、實平此由を九郎御曹司に申す。院御所へ奏聞せられたりければ、
「頼朝に見せて後こそ、ともかうも計らはめ。唯今は爭か許すべき。」と仰ければ、此由を申す。「さらば年來契りたりし聖に、今一度對面して、後世の事を申談ぜばやと思ふはいかゞすべき。」と宣へば、「聖をば誰と申候やらん。」「黒谷の法然房と申人也。」「さては苦しう候まじ。」とて許し奉る。中將斜ならず悦て、聖を請じ奉て、泣々申されけるは、「今度生ながら捕れて候けるは、再上人の見參に罷入べきで候けり。さても重衡が後生いかゞし候べき。身の身にて候し程は、出仕に紛れ、政務にほだされ、驕慢の心のみ深して却て當來の昇沈を顧ず。況や運盡き世亂てより以來は、こゝに戰ひ、かしこに爭ひ、人を滅し身を助らんと思ふ惡心のみ遮て、善心はかつて起らず。就中に南都炎上の事は、王命といひ武命といひ、君に仕へ世に隨ふ法遁かたくして、衆徒の惡行を靜めんが爲に罷向て候し程に、不慮に伽藍の滅亡に及候し事、力及ばぬ次第にて候へども、時の大將軍にて候ひし上は、責め一人に歸すとかや申候なれば、重衡一人が罪業にこそなり候ぬらめと覺え候へ。且はか樣に人しれずかれこれ恥をさらし候もしかしながら其報とのみこそ思知れて候へ。今は首を剃り戒を持なんどして偏に佛道修行したう候へども、かゝる身に罷成て候へば、心に心をもまかせ候はず。今日明日とも知らぬ身の行末にて候へば、如何なる行を修しても、一業助かるべしとも覺えぬこそ口惜う候へ。倩一生の化行を思ふに、罪業は須彌よりも高く、善業は微塵ばかりも蓄へなし。かくて空く命終なば、火血刀の苦果、敢て疑なし。願くは上人慈悲を發し、憐を垂れて、かゝる惡人の助りぬべき方法候はば、示給へ。」其時上人涙に咽て、暫は物も宣はず。良久しう有て、「誠に受難き人身を受ながら、空しう三途に歸り給はん事、悲しんでも猶餘あり。然るを今穢土を厭ひ、淨土を願はんに、惡心を捨てゝ善心を發しましまさん事、三世の諸佛も定て隨喜し給ふらん。それについて出離の道まち／＼なりといへども末法濁亂の機には、稱名を以て勝れたりとす。志を九品に分ち、行を六字に縮めて、如何なる愚癡闇鈍の者も唱るに便あり。罪深ければとて、卑下したまふべからず。十惡五逆囘心すれば往生を遂ぐ。功徳少ければとて、望を絶べからず。一念十念の心を致せば、來迎す。專稱名號至西方と釋して、專名號を稱すれば、西方に至る。念々稱名常懺悔と演て、念々に彌陀を唱れば、懺悔する也と教へたり。利劔即是彌陀號を憑めば、魔縁近づかず。一聲稱念罪皆除と念ずれば、罪皆除けりと見えたり。淨土宗の至極、各略を存して、大略是を肝心とす。但往生の得否は、信心の有無に依べし。唯深く信じて努々疑をなし給ふべからず。もし此教を深く信じて行往座臥時處諸縁を嫌はず三業四威儀に於て、心念口稱を忘れ給はずば、畢命を期として、此苦域の界を出で、彼不退の土に往生し給はん事、何の疑かあらむや。」と教化し給ひければ、中將斜ならず悦て、「此次に戒を持ばやと存候は、出家仕らでは叶候まじや。」と申されければ、「出家せぬ人も、戒を持つ事は世の常の習ひ也。」とて、額に剃刀をあてゝそるまねをして、十戒を授けられければ、中將隨喜の涙を流いて、是を受保ち給ふ。上人も萬物哀に覺えて、掻暗す心地して、泣々戒をぞ説れける。御布施と覺しくて、年比常におはして遊れける侍の許に預置れける御硯を、知時して召寄て、上人に上り、「是をば人にたび候はで、常に御目のかゝり候はん所に置れ候て、某が物ぞかしと、御覽ぜられ候はん度ごとに思食なずらへて御念佛候べし。御隙には經をも一卷、御廻向候はゞ然るべう候べし。」など泣々申されければ、上人とかうの返事にも及ばず、是を取て懷に入れ、墨染の袖を絞りつゝ泣々歸り給ひけり。此の硯は、親父入道相國砂金を多く宋朝の御門へ奉り給ひたりければ返報と覺しくて、日本和田の平大相國の許へとて、送られたりけるとかや。名をば松蔭とぞ申ける。

annotation.translation: The Daisan-no-Chujo, upon hearing this, said, "Indeed, this is what I feared. How could the people of my clan have come to think so ill of me?" Though he regretted it, it was of no avail. Indeed, regretting only the loss of the Minister Shingyo, even though he had not even thought that the Three Sacred Treasures of our Imperial Court, the greatest treasures of the land, should be returned, the purpose of this petition had been conceived long ago. However, before the matter had been fully deliberated, he had felt a certain unease. Now that the petition had arrived and it was decided he must descend to the Eastern Provinces, his strength completely failed, and even the lingering affection for the capital had now faded. The Daisan-no-Chujo summoned Tofu no Jiro and said, "I wish to become a monk; what should be done?" When he spoke thus, Jiro reported this to Prince Hisahira. Since the matter had already been reported to the Imperial Residence, the Emperor said, "Show it to Yoritomo first; we shall not hastily decide the matter now. For the time being, we shall grant permission." Upon hearing this, Jiro reported, "Then, shall we meet once more with the Holy Man, who has been our ally for years, to discuss matters of the afterlife, and if so, what should be done?" The Holy Man asked, "Who is this Holy Man?" "He is Hōnen, a priest of the Kurodani." "Then he shall not be difficult to deal with," and permission was granted. The Chujo was delighted beyond measure. He invited the Holy Man and, weeping, said, "The reason I was captured alive this time was to enable me to pay homage to the Venerable One. Yet, what will become of Shingyo's future life? While I was still alive, I was entangled in official duties, distracted by state affairs, and my heart grew increasingly arrogant, neglecting even the thought of the rise and fall of the coming world. Moreover, since the end of my fortune and the chaos of the world, I have fought here and contended there, thinking only of destroying others to save myself; my evil thoughts have blocked me completely, and no good thoughts have arisen. Especially in the case of the burning of the Southern Capital, whether it was the Imperial Will or the Military Command, the method of serving the ruler and following the world became difficult, and I went to suppress the evil deeds of the monks and lay followers. Yet, unexpectedly, the temple was destroyed. Though I lacked the power to prevent it, as I was the Great General of the time, they said, 'The blame falls solely on you.' Thus, I felt that the sin and karma would rest entirely on Shingyo alone. Moreover, although I have been exposed to such shame before, I only knew it as retribution. Now, though I shave my head and keep precepts, devoting myself solely to Buddhist practice, my body is in such a state that I cannot entrust my heart even to my own mind. For I do not know if today or tomorrow will be my last, and no matter what practice I undertake, I feel no hope that even one deed will save me; this is truly bitter. Reflecting on my life of transformation, my sins are higher than Mount Sumeru, and my good deeds are not even as much as a dust mote. Thus, if I die in vain, the bitter fruit of fire, blood, and swords is beyond doubt. I pray that the Venerable One, having compassion, may show a method by which such an evil person may be saved." At that time, the Venerable One was choked with tears and remained silent for a while. After a long pause, he said, "Truly, to be born in this suffering world and then return empty-handed to the Three Paths is indeed sorrowful, yet there is still hope. However, now that you have renounced this defiled world and aspire to the Pure Land, abandoning evil thoughts and arousing good ones, the Buddhas of the Three Times will surely rejoice with you. Regarding the path of renunciation, though it varies, for the deluded people of the Latter Age of the Dharma, reciting the Name is supreme. Dividing the mind into the Nine Grades and condensing practice into the Six Syllables, even the most ignorant and dull can easily chant. Do not look down on yourself because of deep sin; if one repents the Ten Evils and the Five Heinous Crimes, one attains rebirth. Do not lose hope because of little merit; if one brings forth the mind of one thought or ten thoughts, the Coming of Amitabha occurs. The explanation 'Special Recitation of the Name Leads to the Western Pure Land' means that by solely chanting the Name, one reaches the West. The teaching 'Chanting the Name in Every Thought is Constant Repentance' means that chanting Amitabha in every thought is repentance. Relying on 'The Sharp Sword is the Name of Amitabha' means that evil influences do not approach. Thinking 'One Recitation of the Name Removes All Sins' means that all sins are removed. The essence of the Pure Land Sect is to keep the specifics in mind, but the main point is this: whether one attains rebirth depends on the presence or absence of faith. Only believe deeply and never doubt. If one deeply believes in this teaching and, whether sitting, walking, lying down, or in any situation, does not forget mental or vocal recitation of the Name, then, until the end of one's life, one will leave this realm of suffering and be reborn in the land of non-retrogression. What doubt could there be?" Thus he preached. The Chujo was delighted beyond measure and said, "If I wish to receive the precepts now, should I not become a monk?" The Venerable One replied, "Even those who do not become monks can receive the precepts; this is a common practice in the world." Then, placing a razor on his forehead and pretending to shave, he conferred the Ten Precepts. The Chujo shed tears of joy and received them. The Venerable One, moved by the sorrow of all things, felt as if the world were darkened, and he preached the precepts while weeping. Thinking of it as an offering, the Chujo summoned the inkstone that the Emperor had left in the care of his attendants, who had accompanied him from year to year. He presented it to the Venerable One, saying, "Do not let this pass to others; keep it always where you can see it, so that whenever you look upon it, you may think, 'This is my object,' and chant the Nembutsu. In your spare time, you may also chant a volume of the Sutra and dedicate the merit." Thus he wept and spoke. The Venerable One could not reply in kind; he took the inkstone, placed it in his sleeve, wrung out his ink-stained sleeve, and returned while weeping. This inkstone was sent back as a reward because his father, the Priest, had offered much gold from the Shingō region to the Song Dynasty's imperial gate. It was said to be sent to the residence of the Great Chancellor of the Taira of Wada in Japan. It was named Matsukage.

text: さる程に、本三位中將をば、鎌倉前兵衞佐頼朝、頻に申されければ、さらば下さるべしとて、土肥次郎實平が手より、先九郎御曹司の宿所へ渡し奉る。同三月十日、梶原平三景時に具せられて、鎌倉へこそ下られけれ。西國より生捕にせられ、都へ返るだに口惜きに、今又關の東へ趣かれけん心の中、推量られて哀也。四宮河原に成ぬれば、爰は昔延喜第四の王子、蝉丸の、關の嵐に心を清し、琵琶をひき給ひしに、博雅の三位といひし人、風の吹日も吹ぬ日も、雨の降る夜も降ぬ夜も三年が間歩を運び、立聞て、彼の三曲を傳へけん藁屋の床の古へも、思遣られて哀也。逢坂山を打越えて、勢多の唐橋駒もとゞろに蹈ならし、雲雀あがれる野路の里、志賀の浦浪春かけて霞に曇る鏡山、比良の高峯をも北にして、伊吹の嵩も近附ぬ。心をとむとしなけれども、荒て中中優しきは、不破の關屋の板びさし、如何に鳴海の鹽干潟、涙に袖はしをれつゝ、彼在原のなにがしの、唐ころもきつゝなれにしとながめけん參河國八橋にも成ぬれば、蛛手に物をと哀也。濱名の橋を渡り給へば、松の梢に風亮て、入江に噪ぐ浪の音、さらでも旅は物憂きに、心を盡す夕間暮、池田の宿にも著給ひぬ。彼宿の長者の湯屋が娘、侍從が許に、其夜は宿せられけり。侍從、三位中將を見奉て、「昔は傳にだに思召寄らざりしに、今日はかゝる所にいらせ給ふ不思議さよ。」とて、一首の歌をたてまつる。

annotation.translation: Thus, since Lord Yoritomo, the Kamakura Prefect of the Army, repeatedly requested it, the person in question said, "Then it shall be granted," and handed him over from the hands of Doi Jiro Sanehira to the residence of the First Son, Saki-kyū no Gosho. On the tenth day of the same month, Kajiwara Heizo Kagetoki reported the matter, and he was taken down to Kamakura. "Taken alive from the Western Provinces, it is a bitter regret even to return to the Capital; now again, to be led to the Eastern Provinces, his heart is weighed with suspicion and grief." When he became a thatched hut at Shimonokawa, this place is where, in the fourth year of the Engi era, Prince Senmaru purified his heart in the wind of the Seki Pass, played the biwa, and the person known as the Third Rank of Hakuya, day after day, night after night, for three years, carried the steps, stood listening, and transmitted those three pieces; even the old straw mat of the hut is mourned with grief. Crossing the Awase Mountains, trampling the grass at the Tōbashi Bridge in Seta, the wild goose rises in the field of the village of Nobu; the Shika-no-ura waves stretch to the mist-shrouded Kagami-yama, with the high peaks of Hira to the north, and the height of Ibuki is not yet near. Though one does not turn one's heart, the rough yet gentle boards of the不破 Pass house, how the salt marsh of Nami-no-umi, with tears soaking the sleeves, the one of the Wara family, clad in Tang robes, might have been gazed upon. When he became the Eight Bridges of Mikawa Province, it is a pity to catch things with a spider's hand. Crossing the Hamana Bridge, the wind shines on the pine tips, the sound of waves rustling in the inlet; even so, the journey is melancholy, the evening when the heart is exhausted, he arrived at the inn of Ikeda. The daughter of the innkeeper, the elder of that inn, stayed in the presence of the attendant that night. The attendant, seeing the Third Rank General, said, "In the past, we did not even think of such a thing by hearsay; today, you have come to such a place, what a wonder!" and composed a poem to present.

text: 都を出て日數歴れば、彌生も半過ぎ、春も既に暮なんとす。遠山の花は殘の雪かと見えて、浦々島々かすみ渡り、こし方行末の事共思續け給ふに、「されば是は如何なる宿業のうたてさぞ。」と宣ひて、唯盡せぬものは涙也。御子の一人もおはせぬ事を、母の二位殿も歎き、北の方大納言佐殿も本意なき事にして、萬の神佛に祈申されけれども、其驗なし。「賢うぞ無りける。子だに有ましかば、如何に心苦しかるらん。」と宣ひけるこそ責ての事なれ。佐夜中山にかかり給ふにも、又越べしとも覺えねば、いとゞ哀れの數添て、袂ぞいたく濕まさる。宇都の山邊の蔦の道、心細くも打越えて、手越を過て行けば、北に遠去て、雪白き山あり。問へば甲斐の白根といふ。其時三位中將、落る涙を押てかうぞ思ひ續け給ふ。

annotation.translation: Having left the capital and many days having passed, the second month was already half over, and spring was already drawing to a close. The flowers in the distant mountains appeared to be lingering snow, and mist crossed the bays and islands. As she continued to ponder her fate and future, she said, "Then this must be a terrible karma of some sort." Yet the only thing that could not be stopped were tears. The fact that not even one of her children was present was lamented by the mother, Lady Nidai, and by the Northern Lady, Minister of the Left Sano, who, though they prayed to the myriad gods and Buddhas, their prayers were in vain. "She was so intelligent. If she had even a child, how distressed she would have been," she said; it was this very thing that was the cause of the blame. Even when she was carried to Sano-no-Nakayama, she did not feel that she could cross over, so the number of sorrowful days increased, and her sleeves became thoroughly wet. She passed through the path of wisteria on the mountains of Utsu, a lonely journey, and when she crossed Tego, she went far to the north, where there was a snow-white mountain. When asked, it was said to be Shirane in Kai. At that time, the Captain of the Third Rank, suppressing his falling tears, continued to ponder deeply.

text: 清見が關打過ぎて、富士のすそ野に成ぬれば、北には青山峨々として、松吹く風索々たり。南には蒼海漫々として、岸うつ浪も茫々たり。戀せばやせぬべし、こひせずとも有けりと、明神の歌はしめ給ひける足柄の山をも打越て、こゆるぎの森、鞠子河、小磯、大磯の浦、やつまと、砥上が原、御輿が崎をも打過て、急がぬ旅と思へども、日數やう／＼重なれば、鎌倉へこそ入給へ。

annotation.translation: When Kiyomi passed through Seki and reached the foothills of Mount Fuji, to the north were lofty green mountains, with the pines rustling softly; to the south was a vast blue sea, with waves rolling endlessly against the shore. 'If I love her, I shall waste away,' or 'Even if I do not love her, I shall be here,' so said the shrine's poem. Crossing the mountain of Hakone, where the gods' words were given, one passes through Koyurugi Forest, Mariko River, Koiso, Oiso, Yatsuma, Togarihara, and Mikoshi-ga-saki. Though this journey is not hurried, as the days and nights pile up, one must enter Kamakura.

text: 兵衞佐急ぎ見參して申されけるは、「抑君の御憤を息め奉り、父の恥を雪めんと思ひたちし上は、平家を滅さん事は案の内に候へども、正しく見參に入るべしとは存ぜず候き。此のぢやうでは、八島の大臣殿の見參にも入ぬと覺え候。抑も南都を滅し給ける事は、故太政入道殿の仰にて候しか。又時に取て御計にて候けるか。以外の罪業にこそ候なれ。」と申されければ、三位中將宣ひけるは、「先づ南都炎上の事、故入道の成敗にも非ず、重衡が愚意の發起にもあらず。衆徒の惡行をしづめんが爲に罷向て候し程に、不慮に伽藍滅亡に及候し事、力及ばぬ次第也。昔は源平左右にあらそひて、朝家の御かためなりしかども、近比源氏の運傾きたりし事は事新しう初めて申べきにあらず。當家は保元平治より以來度々の朝敵を平げ、勸賞身に餘り、辱く一天の君の御外戚として、一族の昇進六十餘人、廿餘年の以來は樂み榮え申ばかりなし。今又運盡ぬれば、重衡捕らはれて是まで下候ぬ。それについて帝王の御敵を討たる者は、七代まで朝恩つきせずと申事は、究たる僻事にて候けり。目のあたり故入道殿は、君の御爲に既に命を失はんとする事度々に及ぶ。されども僅に其身一代の幸にて、子孫か樣に罷成るべしや。されば運盡きて都を出し後は、尸を山野にさらし、名を西海の波に流すべしとこそ存ぜしが、是迄下べしとは、かけても思はざりき。唯先世の宿業こそ口惜候へ。但殷湯は夏臺にとらはれ文王はいう里にとらはると云ふ文あり。上古猶かくの如し。況や末代においてをや。弓矢をとる習ひ敵の手にかゝて命を失ふ事、またく恥にて恥ならず。唯芳恩には、疾々かうべをはねらるべし。」とて、其後は物も宣はず。景時是を承て、「あはれ大將軍や。」とて涙を流す。其座に並居たる人々皆袖をぞぬらしける。兵衞佐も、「平家を別して私の敵と思ひ奉る事努々候はず。唯帝王の仰こそ重う候へ。」とぞのたまひける。「南都を亡たる大伽藍の敵なれば、大衆定て申旨在らんずらん。」とて、伊豆國の住人狩野介宗茂に預けらる。其體、冥土にて娑婆世界の罪人を、七日々々に十王の手へ渡さるらんも、かくやと覺て哀也。

annotation.translation: Hyoe-no-sa hurriedly appeared and reported, "Truly, since I had resolved to calm Your Majesty's anger and wash away my father's disgrace, and to destroy the Taira clan, I had considered it inevitable, yet I did not think it appropriate to appear before you properly. Under these circumstances, I fear that I have failed to appear before Minister Yashima. Truly, was it the late Dajō-dōji's command that you destroyed the Southern Capitals? Or was it a plan devised at the right time? Were there not other crimes and sins?" Upon hearing this, the Sanmi no Shōshō declared, "First, the burning of the Southern Capitals was neither a consequence of the late Dōji's downfall nor the foolish idea of Kōchō. It was only when we went to quell the wicked deeds of the monks that, unexpectedly, the temple grounds were destroyed; this was beyond our power. In the past, the Minamoto and Taira clans fought on equal footing, and the Imperial House was their stronghold, but the recent decline of the Minamoto's fortune is not something new that needs to be mentioned for the first time. Our house, since the Genpei and Heiji rebellions, has repeatedly pacified enemies of the court, receiving rewards far exceeding our merit. Humiliatingly, as the Imperial House's maternal relatives, we have seen over sixty members of our family rise in rank; for more than twenty years, we have enjoyed only prosperity and glory. Now, since our fortune has ended, Kōchō has been captured and has come this far. Regarding this, it is said that one who strikes down the Emperor's enemies does not cease to receive imperial favor for seven generations; this is an utterly unreasonable notion. Before our eyes, the late Dōji, for Your Majesty's sake, has repeatedly risked his life. Yet, merely for his own lifetime's fortune, will his descendants be blessed? Therefore, after our fortune ended and we were driven from the capital, I thought we should expose our bodies in the mountains and rivers and let our names flow in the waves of the Western Sea; I never thought we would come this far. Only the karmic sins of our past lives are truly regrettable. However, there is a saying that Tang's Emperor was imprisoned at Xia Tai, and King Wen was imprisoned at Youli. Even in ancient times, it was like this; how much more so in our degenerate age! To take up the bow and arrow, be caught by the enemy's hands, and lose one's life is utterly shameful and disgraceful. Only to the noble grace should we quickly behead ourselves." After this, he said nothing further. Kageyori, hearing this, said, "Alas, the Great General!" and shed tears. All the people sitting together in the assembly moistened their sleeves with their tears. Hyoe-no-sa also said, "I have never considered the Taira clan as my own enemy, separate from others; only the Emperor's command is weighty." He was entrusted to Konno-no-suke Muneshige, a resident of Izu Province. Truly, in the underworld, the sinners of this world will be handed over to the Ten Kings day by day for seven days; thinking of this, it is indeed sorrowful.

text: されども狩野介、情なる者にて、痛く緊しうも當り奉らず、やう／＼に痛り湯殿しつらひなどして、御湯引せ奉る。道すがらの汗いぶせかりつれば、身を清めて失はんずるにこそと思はれけるに、齡二十計なる女房の、色白う清げにて、誠に優に美しきが、目結の帷に、染附の湯卷して、湯殿の戸を推開て參りたり。又暫有て十四五許なる女の童の小村濃の帷きて髮は袙長なるが、楾盥に櫛入て持て參りたる。此女房介錯にて、良久湯あみ髮洗などしてあがり給ひぬ。さて彼女房暇申て歸りけるが、「男などはこちなうもぞ思召す。中々女は苦からじとて、參せられて候ふ。『何事でも思召さん御事をば、承はて申せ。』とこそ兵衞佐殿は仰られ候つれ。」中將、「今は是程の身になて、何事をか申候べき。唯思ふ事とては、出家ぞしたき。」と宣ひければ、歸參て、此由を申す。兵衞佐「其れ思ひも寄らず。頼朝が私の敵ならばこそ。朝敵として預り奉たる人也。努々有るべうもなし。」とぞ宣ひける。三位中將守護の武士に宣ひけるは、「さても唯今の女房は優なりつる者哉。名をば何といふやらん。」と問はれければ、「あれは手越の長者が娘で候を、眉目形、心樣優にわりなき者で候とて、此二三年召仕はれ候が、名をば千手前と申候。」とぞ申ける。

annotation.translation: However, Kano no Suké, being a passionate man, did not endure the pain well and did not come to the bath as he should; instead, he prepared the bathhouse in various ways, such as with pain-relieving herbs, and had the bath drawn. Since he had sweated profusely on the journey, he thought that it would be best to cleanse his body and rid himself of the sweat. A woman of about twenty years, fair-skinned and graceful, truly exceptionally beautiful, appeared, wearing a headband veil and a dyed towel wrapped around her, and opened the door of the bathhouse to enter. After a while, a young girl of about fourteen or fifteen, Komurasaka, came with a veil; her hair was long and wrapped in a double-layered cloth, and she brought a basin and a comb. This woman served as the attendant at the bath; after some time, she washed his hair and bathed him, and he got out. Then, when that woman took her leave and returned, she said, "My lord, you may think men are foolish, but surely women do not suffer in the same way. I have come to serve you. Whatever you may think or desire, please tell me." The Hyoe no Suke replied, "You need not think such thoughts. If Yoshitomo were my enemy, I would have to deal with him as a rebel. There is no way I could ever be so foolish." The Chūjō then spoke to the samurai guarding the Third Lady, saying, "That woman you saw just now was truly exceptional. What is her name?" The guard replied, "She is the daughter of the wealthy man of Tegoshi. Her features and heart are truly admirable. She has been serving in our household for the past two or three years, and her name is Senjō." The Chūjō then returned and reported this to the Third Lady.

Then, when that woman took her leave and returned, she said, "My lord, you may think men are foolish, but surely women do not suffer in the same way. I have come to serve you. Whatever you may think or desire, please tell me." The Hyoe no Suke replied, "You need not think such thoughts. If Yoshitomo were my enemy, I would have to deal with him as a rebel. There is no way I could ever be so foolish." The Chūjō then spoke to the samurai guarding the Third Lady, saying, "That woman you saw just now was truly exceptional. What is her name?" The guard replied, "She is the daughter of the wealthy man of Tegoshi. Her features and heart are truly admirable. She has been serving in our household for the past two or three years, and her name is Senjō." The Chūjō then returned and reported this to the Third Lady.

text: 其夕雨少降て、萬物蕭しかりけるに、件の女房琵琶琴もたせて參たり。狩野介酒をすゝめて奉る。我身も家子郎等十餘人引具して參り、御前近う候けり。千手前酌をとる。中將少しうけて、最興なげにておはしけるを、狩野介申けるは、「且聞思されてもや候らん。鎌倉殿の『相構て能々慰參せよ。懈怠して頼朝恨むな。』と仰られ候[1]宗茂は、伊豆國の者にて候間、鎌倉では旅にて候へども、心の及ばん程は奉公仕候べし。何事でも申てすゝめ參させ給ヘ。」と申ければ、千手酌を差置て、「羅綺の重衣たる情ない事を機婦にねたむ。」と云ふ朗詠を一兩返したりければ、三位中將宣ひけるは、「此朗詠せん人をば、北野天神一日に三度翔て守らんと誓はせ給ふ也。されども重衡は此世では捨られ奉ぬ。助音しても何かせん。罪障輕みぬべき事ならば、隨べし。」とぞ宣ひければ、千手前軈て「十惡と云へ共引攝す。」と云ふ朗詠をして、「極樂願はん人は、皆彌陀の名號唱べし。」と云今樣を四五返うたひすましたりければ、其時盃を傾けらる。千手前給はて狩野介にさす。宗茂がのむ時に、琴をぞ引すましたりける。三位中將宣けるは「此樂をば普通には五常樂といへども、重衡が爲には、後生樂とこそ觀ずべけれ。やがて往生の急を引むと戯れて琵琶を取り、てんじゆをねぢて、皇じやう急をぞ引れける。夜やう／＼深て、萬づ心のすむ儘に、「あら思はずや、吾妻にも是程優なる人の有けるよ。何事にても今一聲。」と宣へば千手前又、「一樹の陰に宿り合ひ、同じ流を掬ぶも、皆是前世の契。」と云ふ白拍子を、誠に面白くかぞへすましたりければ、中將も、「燈暗しては數行虞氏の涙。」と云ふ朗詠をぞせられける。譬へば此朗詠の心は、昔唐土に、漢高祖と楚項羽と位を爭ひて、合戰する事七十二度、戰毎に項羽勝にけり。されども終には、項羽戰負て亡ける時、騅と云ふ馬の一日に千里を飛に乘て、虞氏と云ふ后と共に逃さらんとしけるに、馬如何思ひけん、足をとゝのへて動かず。項羽涙を流いて、「我が威勢既に廢れたり。今は逃るべき方なし。敵の襲ふは事の數ならず、此后に別なん事のかなしさよ。」とて終夜歎き悲み給ひけり。燈暗成ければ心細うて虞氏涙を流す。夜深くる儘に、軍兵四面に閧を作る。此心を橘相公の賦に作るを、三位中將思ひ出されたりしにや、最優うぞ聞えける。

annotation.translation: On that evening, when the rain had fallen a little and all things seemed desolate, the aforementioned lady arrived, carrying a biwa and a koto. Konno no Suke offered wine, saying, "I and my household retainers, numbering over ten, have come to your presence to wait upon you. Please take the cup from Chishu-mae. The Chūjō received it slightly, though he was in a state of utmost sadness. Then Konno no Suke said, 'You may perhaps be thinking of listening to it? Lord Kamakura has commanded: "Take proper care and comfort him well. Do not neglect him, lest Lord Yoritomo bear him a grudge."" Although Sōshige is from Izu Province and is currently a traveler in Kamakura, he should serve you to the best of his ability in any way possible. Please say whatever you wish and let me offer you wine." Upon hearing this, Chishu-mae set down the cup and recited the following rōei: "Jealous of the heartless woman who wears layers of silken robes." The Chūjō responded with this verse: "If this reciter of the rōei were to be found, I would vow that the Kami of Kitano Tenmangū would protect him three times a day. Yet Jūjō cannot be abandoned in this world. Even if I were to pray for him, what would it accomplish? If his sins were light enough to be forgiven, then so be it." Upon hearing this, Chishu-mae immediately recited another rōei: "Though they are called the Ten Evils, they are still restrained." He then sang the current-style song, "Those who wish for Paradise should all chant the name of Amitābha," several times. At that moment, the cup was tilted and handed to Chishu-mae, who then passed it to Konno no Suke. When Sōshige drank, the koto was played to accompany him. The Chūjō declared, "Although this music is generally called the Five Virtues Music, for Jūjō's sake, it should be regarded as the Music of the Afterlife." He then playfully picked up the biwa, as if to hasten the urgency of his rebirth, twisted the tuning pegs, and began to play the "Emperor's Urgent Tune." As the night grew deep, when all his heart's desires were fulfilled, he said, "Alas, I never thought there could be such a gentle person in Azuma! In any matter, let me hear one more voice." Then Chishu-mae, truly amusingly, sang the following Shirabyōshi: "Under the shade of a single tree, we share a dwelling; even scooping water from the same stream is a bond of a former life." The Chūjō then responded with this rōei: "When the lamp is dim, the tears of Yu Shi are but a few lines." For example, the heart of this rōei refers to a time long ago in Tang China, when the Han Emperor Gaozu and the Chu Xiangyu contended for power and fought seventy-two times; each time, Xiangyu emerged victorious. Yet in the end, when Xiangyu was defeated in battle and perished, he attempted to flee with his beloved, Lady Yu, riding his horse named Sui, which could fly a thousand li in a day. But how the horse must have thought, it stopped its feet and would not move. Shedding tears, Xiangyu said, "My power has already been destroyed. Now there is no way to escape. The enemy's attacks are countless; how sorrowful it is that we must part hereafter." Thus, he sighed and mourned throughout the night. When the lamp grew dim, his heart grew fearful, and Lady Yu shed tears. As the night deepened, soldiers surrounded them on all sides, creating a clamor. It was perhaps this very heart, which the Chancellor Tachibana composed in his fu, that the Chūjō recalled, making it sound truly magnificent.

text: さる程に夜も明ければ、武士ども暇申て罷出づ。千手前も歸にけり。其朝兵衞佐殿折節、持佛堂に法華經讀でおはしける處へ、千手前參りたり。兵衞佐殿うちゑみ給ひて、「千手に中人をば面白もしたるもの哉。」と宣へば、齋院次官親義、折節御前に物かいて候けるが、「何事で候けるやらん。」と申。「あの平家の人々は甲冑弓箭の外は他事なしとこそ日比は思ひたれば、此三位中將の琵琶の撥音、口ずさみ、終夜立聞て候に、優にわりなき人にておはしけり。」親義申けるは、「誰も夜部承はるべう候しが、折節痛はる事候て、承らず候。このゝちは常に立聞候べし。平家は本より代々の歌人才人達で候也。先年此人々を花に譬へ候しに、此三位中將殿をば、牡丹の花に譬て候しぞかし。」と申されければ、「誠に優なる人にてありけり。」とて「琵琶の撥音朗詠のやう、後までも有難き事ぞ。」と宣ひける。千手前は中々に物思ひの種とや成にけん。されば中將南都へ渡されて斬れ給ひぬ、と聞えしかば、やがて樣をかへ、濃墨染にやつれ果て、信濃國善光寺に行すまして、彼後世菩提を弔ひ、我身も往生の素懷を遂けるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: As the night passed and dawn broke, the warriors requested permission to retire and departed. Senju-mae had also returned. On that morning, when the Lord of the Hyogo-no-suke was reading the Lotus Sutra in the Maitreya Hall, Senju-mae came to pay his respects. The Lord of the Hyogo-no-suke received him with pleasure and said, "How delightful it is to see a man of Senju-mae's caliber." Upon hearing this, Sainin no Tsukanokimi, who happened to be writing something in the presence of His Lordship, asked, "What is it that you are saying?" Senju-mae replied, "The men of the Taira clan, as far as I know, have nothing to their name but armor and bows and arrows, yet this Lord of the Third Rank, the Middle Captain, with the sound of his lute pick and his humming, has stood and listened to me all night long; he is truly a man of exceptional merit." The Lord of the Hyogo-no-suke responded, "Everyone was eager to hear you last night, but I was suddenly taken ill and could not listen. From now on, I shall always stand and listen. The Taira clan has always been a family of great poets and songwriters. In years past, we compared these people to flowers, and we likened this Lord of the Third Rank, the Middle Captain, to a peony." Upon hearing this, the Lord of the Hyogo-no-suke said, "Truly, he was a man of exceptional merit." He then added, "The sound of his lute pick and his recitation were truly remarkable and will be cherished for generations to come." Senju-mae was deeply moved by these words and became lost in thought. Thus, when it was reported that the Middle Captain had been sent to Nara and beheaded, he immediately changed his appearance, dyed his hair a deep black, and retreated to the Zenko-ji Temple in Shinano Province, where he spent the rest of his days mourning the deceased and fulfilling his wish for rebirth in the Pure Land, as the story goes.

text: さる程に、小松三位中將維盛卿は、身がらは八島にありながら、心は都へ通れけり。故郷に留置給し北方少き人々の面影のみ、身に立そひて、忘るゝ隙も無りければ、「有にかひなき我身かな。」とて、壽永三年三月十五日の曉、忍びつゝ八島の館を紛れ出で、與三兵衞重景、石童丸と云ふ童、船に心得たればとて武里と申舍人、是等三人を召具して、阿波國結城の浦より小舟に乘り、鳴門の浦を漕通り、紀伊路へおもむき給けり。和歌、吹上、衣通姫の神と顯はれ給へる玉津島の明神、日前國懸の御前を過て、紀伊の湊にこそ著給へ。是より山傳ひに都へ上て、戀しき人々を、今一度見もし見えばやとは思へ共、「本三位中將の生捕にせられて大路を渡され、京鎌倉恥をさらすだに口惜きに、此身さへ囚れて、父の尸に血をあやさん事も心うし。」とて、千度心は進め共、心に心をからかひて、高野の御山に參られけり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, although the physical body of the noble Minamoto no Koremori, the Junior Third Rank, was at Yashima, his heart had already passed through to the capital. Only the faces of those few people who had been left behind in his homeland stood before him, and there was no moment to forget them, so he muttered, "Alas, I am utterly worthless." Thus, on the morning of the 15th day of the 3rd month of the 3rd year of Juei, he stealthily slipped away from the mansion at Yashima, summoning Wazaemon Shigeharu, a page named Ishidomaru, and a servant called Takemura, who had prepared a boat, and the three of them boarded a small boat from the port of Yuki in Awa Province. They rowed through the strait of Naruto, heading toward the Kii region. Passing the sacred shrine of Tamatsu-jima, which was revealed as the goddess of the Utsu-hime Shrine at Fukiage, and passing the shrine of Himikuni-no-mimi, they arrived at the port of Kii. From there, ascending the mountain passes to the capital, although he thought, "I wish I could see my beloved ones just one more time," he reflected, "If I were captured alive by the Third Rank, Minamoto no Koremori, and led across the great road, even the shame of exposing myself in Kyoto and Kamakura would be unbearable; moreover, my body being imprisoned would prevent me from even offering my blood to my father's corpse." Thus, though his heart surged a thousand times, he deceived his heart with his heart and went to the sacred mountain of Koya.

text: 高野は年比知給へる聖在り。三條の齋藤左衞門茂頼が子に、齋藤瀧口時頼と云ひし者也。本は小松殿の侍なり。十三の年本所へ參りたりけるが、建禮門院の雜仕横笛と云ふ女あり。瀧口是を最愛す。父是を傳聞いて、「世に有ん者の婿子になして出仕なんどをも、心安うせさせんとすれば、世になき者を思ひ初めて。」と強に諫めければ、瀧口申けるは、「西王母と聞えし人、昔は有て今は無し。東方朔と云し者も、名をのみ聞て目には見ず。老少不定の世の中、石火の光に異ならず、縱人長命といへども、七十八十をば過ず、其中に身の榮んなる事は、僅に廿餘年也。夢幻の世の中に、醜きものを、片時も見て何かせん。思はしき者を見んとすれば、父の命を背くに似たり。是善知識也。しかじ、浮世を厭ひ、實の道に入なん。」とて、十九の年髻切て、嵯峨の往生院に行なひすましてぞ居たりける。横笛是を傳聞いて、「我をこそ捨め、樣をさへ替けん事の恨めしさよ。縱ひ世をば背くとも、などかかくと知せざらむ。人こそ心つよくとも尋ねて恨みむ。」と思ひつゝ、或暮方に都を出で、嵯峨の方へぞあくがれ行く。比はきさらぎ十日餘の事なれば、梅津の里の春風に、餘所の匂もなつかしく、大井河の月影も、霞にこめて朧也。一方ならぬ哀さも、誰故とこそ思ひけめ。往生院とは聞たれども、さだかに何れの坊ともしらざれば、こゝにやすらひ、かしこにたゝずみ、[2]尋ねぬるぞ無慚なる。住荒したる僧房に念誦の聲しけり。瀧口入道が聲と聞なして、「わらはこそ是まで尋ね參りたれ。樣の替りておはすらんをも今一度見奉らばや。」と具したりける女を以て言せければ、瀧口入道、胸打噪ぎ、障子の隙より覗いて見れば、誠に尋かねたる氣色痛敷う覺えて如何なる道心者も、心弱くなりぬべし。やがて人を出して、「全く是にさる人なし。門違でぞあるらむ。」とて終に逢でぞかへしける。横笛情なう恨めしけれども、力なく、涙を押へて歸けり。瀧口入道、同宿の僧に逢て申けるは、「是も世に靜にて、念佛の障碍は候はねども、飽で別し女に、此住ひを見えて候へば、譬ひ一度は心強共、又も慕ふ事あらば、心も動き候べし。暇申て。」とて嵯峨をば出て高野へ上り、清淨心院にぞ居たりける。横笛も樣を替たる由聞えしかば、瀧口入道一首の歌を送けり。

annotation.translation: There was a holy man named Takano, who received an annual allowance. He was the son of Saemon Shumori Shigemochi of Sanjo, who was called Saemon Takaguchi Tokiyori. Originally, he was a retainer of Lord Komatsu. When he was thirteen years old, he went to his native place, where there was a woman named Yokobue, a servant of the Empress Kenrei-mon-in. Takiyori loved her most. His father, having heard of this, strongly remonstrated with him, saying, 'Even if you make a man of no substance in the world your son-in-law and serve as his subordinate, you may find peace of mind; but if you first think of a man of no substance in the world...' However, Takiyori replied, 'The person said to be the Western Queen Mother existed in the past but no longer exists today. The man called Dongfang Shuo, too, is known only by name, not seen with the eyes. In this world where old and young are uncertain, there is no difference from the flash of a stone fire; even if a person lives a long life, he does not pass seventy or eighty years. Among these, the time when one's body prospers is only a little over twenty years. In this world of dreams and illusions, what can one do by seeing an ugly person for even a moment? If one wishes to see a beloved person, it is like turning one's back on one's father's command. This is a good opportunity. Thus, being weary of the floating world, I shall enter the true path.' So, at the age of nineteen, he cut his topknot, went to the Ojo-in of Saga, and lived there. Yokobue, having heard of this, thought, 'How hateful it is that he would abandon me and even change his appearance! Even if he turns his back on the world, how could he not know this? Even if a person has a strong heart, one should search for him and resent him.' With these thoughts, at some twilight, she left the capital and longed to go toward Saga. Since it was about ten days into the second month, the spring wind of Umezu no Sato made the scents of other places seem nostalgic, and the moon's reflection in the Ooi River was hazy, veiled in mist. The extraordinary sadness—why did one think of it as such? Although one had heard of the Ojo-in, one did not know precisely which monastery it was, so one lingered here and stood there, searching without shame. In a dilapidated monk's cell, the sound of chanting was heard. A woman, who had spoken with the words, 'It is I who have searched until now. If only I could see you once more, even though you have changed your appearance,' and presented herself as the voice of the monk Takiyori, was told by the monk, 'My heart is pounding; I peep through the gap of the shoji and see that even any religious devotee would surely become weak-hearted.' He then sent someone out, saying, 'There is certainly no such person here. Perhaps you have come to the wrong gate.' Finally, he sent her away. text: 横笛は、其思ひの積にや奈良の法華寺に有けるが、幾程もなくて、遂にはかなく成にけり。瀧口入道か樣の事を傳へ聞、彌深う行澄して居たりければ、父も不孝を許けり。親しき者ども皆用て、高野の聖とぞ申ける。

text: 三位中將是に尋あひて見給へば、都に候し時は、布衣に立烏帽子、衣文を引繕ひ、鬢を撫で、花やかなりし男士也。出家の後は、今日初て見給ふに、未だ三十にもならぬが、老僧姿に痩衰へ、濃墨染に同じ袈裟、思入れたる道心者、羨敷や思はれけん。晉の七賢、漢の四晧が栖けん商山竹林の有樣も、是には過じとぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: The Vice-Captain of the Third Rank, when he came to inquire and see, was, in the days he was in the capital, wearing a commoner's robe and a black cap, his sleeves drawn and mended, his temples smoothed, a man as lovely as a flower. After his ordination, when you saw him today for the first time, though he was not yet thirty, he had grown thin and frail in the appearance of an old monk, wearing a cassia-dyed robe as dark as ink-dye, a man of deep religious conviction; one might well have felt envy. The Seven Sages of Jin and the Four Worthies of Han, who resided in the Shangshan and the Bamboo Grove, it seemed to me, did not surpass this man.

text: 瀧口入道、三位中將を見奉り、「こは現共覺え候はぬ者哉。八島より是迄は何として逃させ給て候やらん。」と申ければ、三位中將宣ひけるは、「さればとよ、人なみ／＼に、都を出て、西國へ落下りたりしかども、故郷に留置し少者共の戀しさ、いつ忘るべしとも覺えねば、其物思ふ氣色の言ぬにしるくや見えけん、大臣殿も、二位殿も、此人は池大納言の樣に、二心有りなどとて思ひ隔て給ひしかば、有にかひなき吾身哉と、いとゞ心も留まらであくがれ出てこれまではのがれたるなり。如何にもして山傳ひに都へ上て戀しき者共を今一度見もし見えばやとは思へども、本三位中將の事口惜ければ其も叶はず。同くは是にて出家して、火の中水の底へも入ばやと思ふ也。但熊野へ參らんと思ふ宿願あり。」と宣へば、「夢幻の世の中は、とてもかくても候なん。長き世の闇こそ心うかるべう候へ。」とぞ申ける。やがて瀧口入道先達にて、堂塔巡禮して、奧院へ參り給ふ。

annotation.translation: The Taki-guchi Nyudo, seeing the Sanmi-no-Chujo, said, "Is this not a person who has not realized the truth even in this life? How could he have escaped from the Yashima all the way to here?" Upon hearing this, the Sanmi-no-Chujo replied, "Indeed, although many have left the capital and fled to the Western Provinces, I cannot forget my longing for the children left behind in my native land; I cannot recall ever forgetting such feelings. Yet, because the Dainagon-sama and the Ni-i-sama thought of this man as having two hearts, like the Ike-no-Dainagon, and held him in suspicion, I felt that my own life was utterly worthless, and with my heart even more unsettled, I escaped in this very manner. Although I deeply wish to ascend to the capital again, crossing the mountains, and once more see those whom I miss, I cannot fulfill this wish, for it would be regrettable to the Sanmi-no-Chujo. Therefore, I intend to become a monk here, wishing to enter even the fire or the depths of water. However, I have a lifelong vow to visit Kumano." Upon hearing this, he said, "The world of dreams and illusions is like this, no matter what. The long darkness of this life is indeed what one should be concerned about." Then, the Taki-guchi Nyudo led the way, they toured the temples and shrines, and went to the Oku-in.

text: 高野山は帝城を去て二百里、京里を離て無人聲、晴嵐梢を鳴して、夕日の影靜也。八葉の峰、八の谷、誠に心も澄ぬべし。花の色は林霧の底に綻び、鈴の音は尾上の雲に響けり。瓦に松生ひ、墻に苔むして、星霜久く覺えたり。抑延喜帝の御時、御夢想の御告有て、檜皮色の御衣を參らせられしに、勅使中納言資澄卿、般若寺僧正觀賢を相具して、此御山に參り、御廟の扉を開いて、御衣を著せ奉らんとしけるに、霧厚く隔たて、大師拜まれさせ給はず。こゝに觀賢深く愁涙して、「我悲母の胎内を出て、師匠の室に入しより以來いまだ禁戒を犯せず。さればなどか拜奉らざらん。」とて五體を地に投げ、發露啼泣し給ひしかば、漸霧晴て、月の出が如くして、大師拜まれ給けり。時に觀賢隨喜の涙を流いて、御衣を著せ奉る。御ぐしの長く生させ給ひたりしかば、剃奉るこそめでたけれ。勅使と僧正とは拜み奉給へども、僧正の弟子石山の内供淳祐、其時は未童形にて供奉せられたりけるが、大師を拜み奉らずして、嘆き沈で御座けるが、僧正手をとて、大師の御膝に押當られたりければ、其手一期が間、香しかりけるとかや。其移り香は、石山の聖教に移て今に有とぞ承る。大師御門の御返事に申させ給ひけるは、「我昔薩たに逢て、まの當り悉印明を傳ふ。無比の誓願を發して、邊地の異域に侍り。晝夜に萬民を哀んで、普賢の悲願に住す。肉身に三昧を證して、慈氏の下生を待つ。」とぞ申させ給ひける。彼摩訶迦葉の鶏足の洞に籠て、翅頭の春の風を期し給ふらんも、かくやとぞ覺えける。御入定は承和二年三月二十一日寅の一點の事なれば、過にし方も三百餘歳、行末も猶五十六億七千萬歳の後、慈尊出世三會の曉を待せ給ふらんこそ久しけれ。

annotation.translation: Koya-san lies two hundred ri from the imperial capital, separated from the outskirts of Kyoto by silence; the clear misty peaks sing through the treetops, and the shadow of the setting sun is still. Eight leaves of peaks, eight valleys; truly, the heart can become clear. The color of flowers blooms at the bottom of the forest mist; the sound of bells resounds in the clouds above O-no. Pines grow on the tiles, moss covers the walls; the stars and frost have long been remembered. In the time of Emperor En'yū, a divine dream appeared, and he was granted the privilege of wearing a robe of cypress-bark color. The imperial envoy, the Chancellor of State Sukezane, accompanied by the High Priest Kannon of Hōnō-ji, visited this holy mountain, opened the door of the imperial mausoleum, and intended to place the robe upon it, but the fog was thick and barred the way, preventing the Great Master from being worshipped. Thereupon, Kannon, deeply sorrowful and weeping, said, "Since I left my mother's womb and entered my master's quarters, I have never violated the precepts. Why then should I not pay my homage?" Casting his body to the ground, he confessed his faults, wept aloud, and in due course the fog gradually cleared, the moon appeared as if rising, and the Great Master was worshipped. At that time, Kannon, shedding tears of joy, had the robe placed upon him. Because the robe had been granted to grow long, it was deemed fitting to shave it. Although the imperial envoy and the high priest paid their respects, the high priest's disciple, Jūyū, the Inner Attendant of Ishiyama, who at that time was still a child and had been assigned to serve, did not pay homage to the Great Master but sighed and sat in sorrow. The high priest took his hand and pressed it against the Great Master's knee; for a moment, that hand smelled fragrant. It is said that this transferred fragrance remains in the sacred teachings of Ishiyama to this day. In reply to the Great Master's gate, he spoke thus: "Long ago I met him in Sata, and he personally transmitted the complete dharani of the Seal of All. I made an incomparable vow to reside in a distant, foreign land. Day and night I grieved for the ten thousand people, dwelling in the compassionate vow of Samantabhadra. I attained samadhi in this physical body, waiting for the descent of Maitreya." It is said that he was thus speaking. When he secluded himself in the cave of the chicken's foot of Mahākāśyapa, waiting for the spring wind of the head of the wing, it was as if he felt this. Since his entry into samadhi occurred on the twenty-first day of the third month of the second year of Jōwa, at the hour of the tiger, the past has already passed by over three hundred years; and even after the end of his conduct, still five hundred sixty-seven million years later, he will surely await the dawn of the Three Assemblies of the Descent of the Merciful One. How long that will be!

text: 「維盛が身の何となく、雪山の鳥の啼らんやうに、今日よ明日よと思ふものを。」とて、涙ぐみ給ぞ哀なる。鹽風に黒み、盡せぬ物思に痩衰て、其人とは見え給はねども、猶世の人には勝れ給へり。其夜は瀧口入道が庵室に歸て終夜、昔今の物語をぞし給ひける。聖が行儀を見給へば、至極甚深の床の上には、眞理の玉を磨くらむと見えて、後夜晨朝の鐘の聲には、生死の眠をさますらむとも覺えたり。のがれぬべくはかくてもあらまほしうや思はれけん。明ぬれば、東禪院の智覺上人と申ける聖を請じ奉て、出家せんとし給ひけるが、與三兵衞、石童丸を召て宣ひけるは、「維盛こそ人しれぬ思ひを身に副ながら、道狹う遁れ難き身なれば、空しうなるとも、此比は世に有る人こそ多けれ。汝等は如何なる有樣をしてもなどかすぎざるべき。我如何にもならぬ樣を見果て急ぎ都へ上り、各が身をも助け、且は妻子をも育み、且は又維盛が後生をも弔らへかし。」と宣へば、二人の者共、さめ％＼と泣いて、暫は御返事にも及ばず、稍有て與三兵衞涙を押へて申けるは、「重景が父與三左衞門景康は、平治の逆亂の時、故殿の御供に候けるが、二條堀河の邊にて、鎌田兵衞に組んで、惡源太に討たれ候ぬ。重景もなじかは劣り候べき。其時は未二歳に罷成候ければ、少も覺え候はず。母には七歳で後れ候ぬ。あはれをかくべき親しい者、一人も候はざりしかども、故大臣殿、『あれは我命にかはりたりし者の子なれば。』とて、御前にてそだてられ參せ、生年九と申し時、君の御元服候し夜、首を取上られまゐらせて、辱く『盛の字は家の字なれば五代につく。重の字をば松王に。』と仰候て、重景とは付られ參せて候也。其上童名を松王と申ける事も生れて忌五十日と申し時父がいだいてまゐりたれば此家を小松といへば祝うてつくるなりと仰候て松王とはつけられまゐらせ候也。父のようて死候けるも、我身の冥加と覺え候。隨分同隷共にも芳心せられてこそ罷過候しか。されば御臨終の御時も、此世の事をば思召捨て、一事も仰候はざりしかども、重景を御前近う召されて、『あな無慚や、汝は重盛を父が形見と思ひ、重盛は汝を景康が形見と思ひてこそ過しつれ。今度の除目に靱負尉になして、己が父景康を呼し樣に召ばやとこそ思つるに、空しうなるこそ悲しけれ、相構て、少將殿の心に違ふな。』とこそ仰せ候しか。されば日比はいかなる御事も候はむには見捨參せて落べき者と思召し候けるか。御心の中こそ慚しう候へ。『此比は世に有る人こそ多けれ。』と仰蒙り候は、當時の如くは、皆源氏の郎等共こそ候なれ。君の神にも佛にも成らせ給ひ候なむ後樂み榮え候とも、千年の齡を歴べきか。縱萬年を保つとも終には終りの無るべきか。是に過たる善知識何事か候べき。」とて、手づから髻切て、泣々瀧口入道に剃らせけり。石童丸も是を見て、髻際より髮をきる。是も八つより附奉て、重景にも劣ず、不便にし給ければ、同瀧口入道に剃らせけり。是等がか樣に先立てなるを見給ふにつけても、いとど心細うぞ思食す。さても有るべきならねば、流轉三界中、恩愛不能斷、棄恩入無爲、眞實報恩者。」と三反唱給ひて、終に剃下し給てけり。「あはれ替ぬ姿を戀しき者共に今一度見えもし見えて後、かくもならば思ふ事あらじ。」と宣ひけるこそ罪ふかけれ。三位中將も與三兵衞も同年にて今年は廿七歳也。石童丸は十八にぞ成ける。

annotation.translation: "I wonder what has become of Norimori; like a bird crying in the snow mountains, thinking 'today or tomorrow,'" he said, tears filling his eyes, looking most sorrowful. His face darkened by the salt wind, he had grown thin from endless longing; though he no longer looked like himself, he still surpassed ordinary people of the world. That night he returned to the hut of the Taki-guchi Priest and spent the entire night recounting tales of past and present. When the Holy One beheld his conduct, it appeared as though he were polishing the Jewel of Truth on the very deepest bed of enlightenment; at the sound of the night and morning bells, it seemed as though he were awakening from the sleep of life and death. "Yet, even so, I wished I could escape." When dawn broke, he requested the Holy One known as Chishaku of Tōzen-in to ordain him, but Yūzaemon summoned Ishidamaru and declared: "Norimori, though burdened with a hidden sorrow, is in a narrow path from which escape is difficult; even if it proves vain, there are many people like this in the world today. You, too, should not linger in such a state. I, having seen the end of my own hopeless condition, will hasten back to the capital, save myself, raise my wife and children, and also mourn for Norimori's future." Upon hearing this, the two men wept bitterly and could not reply for a while. After a pause, Yūzaemon, suppressing his tears, said: "Shigeharu's father, Yūzaemon Kageyasu, served the late Lord during the rebellion of Hōgen. By the side of Nijō Horikawa, he engaged in combat with Kamada Bēmon and was slain by Gengorō. Shigeharu, too, must have been equally loyal. At that time, he was only two years old and remembered nothing. He was seven years old when his mother died. Though there was no one as dear to him as a parent to grieve for, the late Minister said, 'For he is the child of one who took my place,' and had him raised before the Lord's presence. When he turned nine, on the night of the Lord's coming-of-age ceremony, his head was shaved, and shamefully he was told, 'The character 'Mori' is the family name, used for five generations. Let us give him the character 'Shige' instead.' Thus he was named Shigeharu. Furthermore, when his childhood name was given as Matsuwō, his father held him in his arms on the fiftieth day after his birth, saying, 'Since this house is called Komatsu, we celebrate and name him Matsuwō.' He was named Matsuwō in that way. Though my father died like him, I felt it was my own fortune. Even among our humble servants, he was held in high regard. Therefore, even at his deathbed, though he abandoned all thoughts of this world and said nothing, he summoned Shigeharu close and said, 'Alas, how shameless! You thought of Shigemori as your father's legacy, and Shigemori thought of you as Kageyasu's legacy. text: 良有て、舍人武里を召て、「おのれはとう／＼是より八島へ歸れ。都へは上るべからず。其故は、終には隱れあるまじけれ共、正しう此有樣を聞ては、やがて樣をも替んずらんと覺ゆるぞ。八島へ參て、人々に申さんずるやうはよな、『かつ御覽候し樣に、大方の世間も懶き樣に罷り成候き。萬づ無道さも數添て見え候しかば、各々にも知られ參せ候はでかく成候ぬ。西國で左中將失候ぬ。一谷で備中守うたれ候ぬ。我さへかく成候ぬれば、如何に各の便なう思召され候はんずらむと、それのみこそ心苦しう思ひまゐらせ候へ。抑唐皮と云ふ鎧、小烏と云ふ太刀は、平將軍貞盛より、當家に傳へて、維盛迄は嫡々九代に相當る。若不思議にて世も立なほらば六代に給ぶべし。』と申せ。」とこそ宣ひけれ。武里「君の如何にもならせおはしまさん樣を見參せて後こそ、八島へも參り候はめ。」と申ければ、「さらば。」とて召具せらる。瀧口入道をも善知識の爲に具せられけり。山伏修業者の樣にて高野をば出て、同國の内山東へこそ出られけれ。藤代の王子を始めとして、王子王子伏拜み參り給ふ程に、千里の濱の北、岩代王子の御前にて、狩裝束なる者七八騎が程行逢奉る。既に搦捕れなむずと思ひて、各腰の刀に手をかけて腹を切らむとし給けるが、近附けれども、過つべき氣色も無て急ぎ馬より下深う畏て通りければ、「見知たる者にこそ、誰なるらん。」と怪くて、いとゞ足早にさし給ふ程に、是は當國の住人、湯淺權守宗重が子に湯淺七郎兵衞宗光といふ者也。郎等共「是は如何なる人にて候やらむ。」と申ければ、七郎兵衞涙をはらはらと流いて「あら事も辱なや、あれこそ小松大臣殿の御嫡子三位中將殿よ。八島より是までは何として逃させ給ひたりけるぞや。はや御樣を替させ給てけり。與三兵衞、石童丸も同く出家して、御供申たり。近う參て、見參にも入たかりつれども、憚もぞ思召すとて通りぬ。あなあはれの御有樣や。」とて、袖を顏に押あてて、さめ％＼と泣ければ、郎等共も皆涙をぞながしける。

annotation.translation: Yoshiyori summoned Yorimura and said, 'Go back to the Eight Islands from here. You must not return to the capital. The reason is that although you will inevitably have to hide in the end, if you hear this situation properly, you will surely feel that your appearance will soon change. It is better to go to the Eight Islands and tell the people, "Just as Your Majesty has seen, the world at large has become lazy. Because all manner of injustice has become visible, everyone has come to know of it. The Middle Captain was lost in the Western Provinces. The Bitchu no Kami was killed at Ichitani. Even I have come to such a state; how could everyone possibly think it convenient for you? Only this is what makes my heart ache." Moreover, the armor called Karamokake and the sword called Kogarasu were handed down from the Taira General Sadamori to our house, and up to Yoshimori, they have been passed down through nine generations in direct succession. If, contrary to expectation, the world were to be set right again, they would have been handed down for six generations.' So he said. Yorimura replied, 'After I have had the honor of seeing Your Majesty in such a state, only then shall I go to the Eight Islands.' So he was summoned and prepared his gear. Even Takiguchi Nyūdō was prepared for the sake of a good friend. Dressed as a mountain ascetic, he left Kōya and emerged into the same province's Mount Yamada. Starting with the Fujidaira no Ōji, he received the prostrations of many Ōji, and as he proceeded, he encountered about seven or eight riders in hunting attire at the north of the Thousand-Mile Beach, before the shrine of the Iwashiro no Ōji. Thinking they would surely be captured, they each placed their hands on the swords at their waists, intending to cut their bellies. However, as they approached, they showed no intention of passing by; instead, they quickly dismounted from their horses, bowed deeply, and passed by. 'Only if they were someone we know,' he wondered, 'who could they be?' As he hurried on even more, he realized that this was a local resident, Yusa Gon no Kami Muneshige's son, Yusa Shichirōbei Mutsunori. His retainers asked, 'Who might this person be?' Shichirōbei, with tears streaming down his face, said, 'Oh, what a shameful thing! That is indeed the Third Rank, the Middle Captain, the legitimate son of Lord Minister Komatsu. How did he manage to escape from the Eight Islands up to here? He has already changed his appearance. Goemon and Ishidomaru also took the tonsure and served as his companions. I had intended to approach and pay my respects, but I feared he might be offended, so I passed by. Oh, what a pitiful state he is in!' Then, pressing his sleeve to his face, he wept bitterly, and all the retainers wept as well.

text: 漸さし給ふ程に日數歴れば岩田河にも懸り給ひけり。此川の流を一度も渡る者は、惡業煩惱無始の罪障消なるものをと、憑敷うぞおぼしける。本宮に參りつき證誠殿の御前につい居給ひつゝ暫く法施參せて、御山の體を拜み給に、心も詞も及ばれず。大悲擁護の霞は、熊野山にたなびき、靈驗無雙の神明は、音無河に跡を垂る。一乘修行の岸には、感應の月曇もなく、六根懺悔の庭には、妄想の露も結ばず。何れも／＼憑からずといふ事なし。夜深け人靜て、啓白し給ふに、父の大臣の、此御前にて、命を召して後世を扶け給へと、申されける事までも、思召出て哀也。「本地阿彌陀如來にてまします。攝取不捨の本願誤たず、淨土へ導給へ。」と申されける中にも、「故郷に留置し妻子安穩に。」と祈られけるこそ悲しけれ。浮世を厭ひ眞の道に入給へども、妄執は猶盡ずと覺えて、哀なりし事共也。

annotation.translation: As he began to do so, the days passed, and he had already reached Iwata River. He believed that whoever crossed this river even once would have their evil karma, afflictions, and sins from beginningless time extinguished. Upon arriving at the main palace, he remained before the Shōjō Hall, briefly receiving a Dharma sermon, and then worshipped the body of the mountain, yet his heart and words could not suffice. The mist of Great Compassionate protection hung over Mount Kuma, and the incomparable divine spirit left its traces in the Otozu River. At the shore of One-Vehicle practice, there was no clouding of the moon of response; in the courtyard of the six senses' repentance, no dew of delusion formed. There was nothing in the world that did not arise from attachment. As the night grew deep and people fell silent, he made his declaration: 'Even the very words that he requested, "After my life is taken before this hall, please guide me to the next world,"' arose in his mind, bringing sorrow. 'I am the Original Ground, Amitābha Tathāgata. Do not err in the primal vow of embracing and never abandoning; guide me to the Pure Land.' Yet amidst these words, the prayer, 'Please leave me in my homeland, and ensure the safety of my wife and children,' was all the more sorrowful. Though he had turned away from the floating world and entered the true path, he felt that his delusive attachments were not yet exhausted, and such things were sorrowful.

text: 明ぬれば、本宮より舟に乘り、新宮へぞ參られける。神藏を拜み給に、巖松高く聳えて嵐妄想の夢を破り、流水清く流て、浪塵埃の垢をすゝぐらんとも覺たり。明日の社伏拜み、佐野の松原さし過て、那智の御山に參給ふ。三重に漲り落る瀧の水、數千丈まで打上り、觀音の靈像は岩の上に顯れて、補陀落山とも謂つべし。霞のそこには法華讀誦の聲聞ゆ、靈鷲山とも申つべし。抑權現當山に跡を垂させまし／＼てより以來、我朝の貴賤上下歩を運び首を傾け掌を合せて利生に關らずといふことなし。僧侶されば甍を竝、道俗袖を連ぬ。寛和の夏の比、花山法皇、十善の帝位を逃させ給ひて、九品の淨刹を行はせ給ひけん御庵室の舊跡には、昔を忍ぶと覺しくて、老木の櫻ぞ開にける。

annotation.translation: When dawn broke, he boarded a boat from the Main Palace and went to the New Palace. Paying reverence to the Kannon, the Iwamatsu rose high, shattering the dream of stormy delusions; the flowing water ran clear, washing away the dust of the waves, though one might think it merely a dream. He paid his respects at the shrine of tomorrow, passed through the pine groves of Sano, and went to Mount Nachi. The water of the waterfall, swelling in three tiers, rose up to thousands of feet; the spiritual image of Kannon appeared upon the rock, and this could be called Mount Potalaka. There, amidst the mist, the sound of chanting the Lotus Sutra can be heard; this too may be called Mount Girisika. In short, since the time when the Gongen left his traces at this mountain, in our imperial age, high and low, rich and poor, have all walked, bowed their heads, and clasped their hands, with nothing that does not concern the salvation of beings. Monks stand shoulder to shoulder; laypeople and monks link sleeves. In the summer of the Kanwa era, Emperor Kaza fled the throne of the Ten Virtues and traveled to the nine grades of the Pure Land. On the old site of his hermitage, feeling as if the past were before one's eyes, the cherry blossoms of the old tree bloomed.

text:
那智籠の僧共の中に、此三位中將を能々見知奉たると覺くて、同行に語りけるは、
「こゝなる修業者を如何なる人やらむと思ひたれば、小松大臣殿の御嫡子、三位中將
殿にておはしけるぞや。あの殿の未だ四位少將と聞え給ひし安元の春の比、法住寺殿
にて五十の御賀のありしに、父小松殿は内大臣の左大將にてまします。伯父宗盛卿は
中納言右大將にて、階下に著座せられたり。其外三位中將知盛、頭中將重衡以下、一
門の人々今日を晴と時めき給ひて、垣代に立給ひし中より、此三位中將殿櫻の花をか
ざして、青海波を舞ていでられたりしかば、露に媚たる花の御姿、風に飜る舞の袖、
地を照し天も耀くばかり也。女院より關白殿を御使にて、御衣をかけられしかば、父
の大臣座をたち是を給はて、右の肩にかけ、院を拜し奉り給ふ。面目類少うぞ見えし。かたへの殿上人も、如何許羨敷う思はれけむ。内裏の女房達の中には、深山木の中の楊梅とこそ覺ゆれなど言れ給ひし人ぞかし。唯今大臣の大將待かけ給へる人とこそ見奉りしに、今日はかくやつれ果給へる御有樣、兼ては思寄ざりしをや。移れば替る世の習ひとは云ひながら、哀なる御事哉。」とて、袖を顏に推當て、さめ％＼と泣ければ、幾等も並居たる那智籠りの僧共も、みなうち衣の袖をぞぬらしける。

annotation.translation: Among the monks of Nachi-no-kago, one who had closely observed and come to know this Sanmi no Chunagon said to his fellow travelers, 'Because I wished to know what sort of person this ascetic here might be, I heard he is the eldest son of the Great Minister Komatsu, Sanmi no Chunagon-dono. Back in the spring of Angen, when he was still known as Shino no Shousho, there was a celebration for his fiftieth birthday at Hozon-ji Temple. At that time, his father, the Great Minister Komatsu, was serving as the Dainagon and Sadaijin. His uncle, Suke-mori-no-kyo, was the Chunagon and Udaijin, and was seated in the ranks below. Besides these, Sanmi no Chunagon Tomomori, the Head Chunagon Shigezane, and others of the family were enjoying their current glory and standing by the hedge. From among them, this Sanmi no Chunagon-dono, wearing cherry blossoms in his hair and dancing with the blue-green waves, appeared so that his face, charming like a flower with dew, and his sleeves fluttering in the wind, seemed to illuminate the earth and shine the heavens. The Nyoin sent the Kampaku-dono as her envoy, and he was bestowed with robes. The Great Minister left his seat and gave them to him; he draped them over his right shoulder, bowed to the Nyoin, and presented them. His appearance was so strikingly handsome that all the courtiers nearby must have thought it utterly enviable. Among the ladies-in-waiting of the Imperial Palace, there were those who said, "He is like a bayberry in the deep mountains." I had seen him as the very person the Great Minister and the Daijo were waiting for, yet today he appears so worn out, a sight I never could have imagined. Although they say it is the custom of the world to change and replace, how sorrowful it is!' Saying this, he pressed his sleeve to his face and wept bitterly; and the monks of Nachi-no-kago, who had been sitting nearby in a row, all wetted the sleeves of their robes with their tears.
